body:
Older adults who get primary care at about 150 CenterWell Senior Primary Care clinics will soon have a new majority owner behind their doctor's office. Humana announced on Oct. 13 that funds managed by HPS Investment Partners, part of BlackRock, will buy private equity firm Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe's stake in the clinics, a stake valued at about $2.8 billion.

The news came two days before Medicare's annual open enrollment period began on Oct. 15, when millions of seniors review their health coverage. CenterWell will remain a minority owner and keep managing the clinics, and Humana says there will be no changes to patient care, according to Healthcare Dive's report on the joint venture.

The deal has not closed yet. It is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and state and federal regulatory approval.

Inside the BlackRock Deal

According to Humana's announcement filed with federal securities regulators, BlackRock will hold the majority stake in a new joint venture, while CenterWell will hold a minority stake and continue to operate the clinics. The new venture replaces two earlier joint ventures with Welsh Carson, which Humana first formed in 2020 and expanded in 2022.

Under the old arrangement, Welsh Carson held a put option that could have required Humana to buy back its stake. The new venture has no put option, which Humana expects to significantly reduce its balance sheet liabilities. BlackRock will receive certain protections instead. Starting in 2028, CenterWell may buy clinics back from the venture. If it has not bought all of them by the end of 2033, BlackRock can exit through a sale, with CenterWell getting the first right to make an offer on the remaining clinics.

Over the next two years, the venture plans to invest in current clinic operations, new clinics, and acquisitions. Humana said it expects "a significantly lower cost of capital" under the new joint venture, reflecting the maturity of the business, according to Fierce Healthcare's coverage of the deal. The company does not expect the deal to materially affect its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance.

"We look forward to this new venture with BlackRock as our partner," said Dr. Sanjay Shetty, president of CenterWell.

The deal is Humana's second with BlackRock this year, following an agreement to sell its minority stake in home health company Gentiva to a group of investors that includes BlackRock. Humana has been working through a financial turnaround after higher-than-expected medical spending squeezed its results, which helps explain its interest in cheaper capital for the clinics. In a note to investors, J.P. Morgan analyst Lisa Gill said investors will look for details on CenterWell's performance, the deal's terms, and the protections BlackRock receives.

Patient Care Under a New Owner

CenterWell's broader primary care network is larger than the clinics in this deal. CenterWell and its sister brand, Conviva Senior Primary Care, now operate more than 350 senior primary care locations, Healthcare Dive reported. As of the end of 2024, the two brands had more than 340 centers in 15 states, including Florida, Texas, Georgia, Arizona, and North Carolina, and served about 390,000 seniors, according to a February 2025 Humana release on CenterWell's planned expansion. That release says the centers accept Original Medicare and a wide range of Medicare Advantage plans.

CenterWell describes its clinics as senior-focused, value-based primary care. In general, value-based care pays providers based on how well they manage patients' overall health and costs, rather than only for each visit or service.

Humana's statement that care will not change is a company commitment, not an independent finding. There is no outside data yet on how this specific deal will affect patients. Because CenterWell will keep running the clinics, the most likely areas to watch over time are which clinics expand or close and how quickly new locations open.

Welsh Carson has put at least $1.8 billion into the venture since its first investment in 2020, according to STAT's report on the BlackRock buyout, which noted that the timing fits a private equity firm looking to exit.

Questions Seniors and Caregivers Can Ask

The people most likely to notice any effects are seniors with Medicare Advantage plans who rely on a CenterWell doctor, older adults with several chronic conditions who need frequent visits, and caregivers who coordinate appointments and referrals.

During open enrollment, which runs from Oct. 15 to Dec. 7, patients can ask their clinic a few direct questions. Will my doctor stay with this clinic next year? Which Medicare plans will the clinic accept in 2027? Will my specialists and hospital referrals stay the same? Will the billing name or patient portal change?

Seniors should also confirm that their current doctor is in network for any plan they are considering, using Medicare's online plan finder tool or by calling the plan directly. Free, unbiased help is available through each state's State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) and through 1-800-MEDICARE. People with Original Medicare face fewer network questions because they can generally see any doctor who accepts Medicare.

Caregivers can keep a simple file with the patient's medication list, recent test results, and specialist contacts, which can make any future change in doctors or clinics less disruptive. Patients who notice longer waits, canceled appointments, or a doctor leaving can raise concerns with the clinic and their health plan, and with Medicare if problems continue.

Next comes regulatory review, with closing expected before the end of the year. Humana is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 6, when analysts may press for more details on CenterWell's plans. For now, patients do not need to take any action because of the deal, but open enrollment is a good time to confirm that their doctor and plan will still work together in 2027.

What is happening to CenterWell clinics? Funds managed by BlackRock's HPS Investment Partners will take a majority stake in about 150 CenterWell Senior Primary Care clinics, buying out private equity firm Welsh Carson's stake, valued at about $2.8 billion. CenterWell will keep managing the clinics as a minority owner.

Will my CenterWell doctor change? Humana says there will be no changes to patient care. Ask your clinic directly whether your doctor will remain there in 2027.

When does the deal take effect? It is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to state and federal regulatory approval.

Does CenterWell accept Original Medicare? According to Humana, CenterWell centers accept Original Medicare and a wide range of Medicare Advantage plans. Confirm coverage for your specific plan.

What should I do during open enrollment? Between Oct. 15 and Dec. 7, check that your doctor is in network for any plan you choose, using Medicare's plan finder or your state's free counseling program.

Where can I get unbiased Medicare help? Call 1-800-MEDICARE or contact your State Health Insurance Assistance Program for free counseling.
